target_customer: Veterinary practices and veterinarians (and pet owners filling prescriptions)
problem: Veterinary prescriptions were handled by phone, fax and paper; vets lacked e-prescribing tied to pharmacies.
business_model: Software for vet practices to e-prescribe and run a practice-branded online pharmacy; also operated a retail veterinary pharmacy (trademark filings cover retail and online veterinary pharmacy services)

founders.name: Georgia Jeremiah
founders.background_notes: Described on YC page as a veterinarian.

technical_complexity.rationale: E-prescribing UI plus pharmacy fulfilment integrations; standard engineering, with licensing and logistics rather than technology as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Practice workflow integration could create stickiness, but no evidence either way; the company also needed pharmacy licensing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying documented in sources reached. The SEC prospectus of Wag! Group says Wag! closed the all-stock Furmacy acquisition on 2022-10-24 (90,000 shares, valued at $283 thousand, described as not material); a 2023 news item reported Wag! closed the El Dorado Hills pet pharmacy afterwards.

market_need_then: A veterinarian co-founder indicates first-hand pain with phone, fax and paper prescriptions; Covetrus and others already sold practice-branded online pharmacy products. No dated demand source (2020-21) was found.

identity.logo: An image mark was filed with the USPTO in April 2024; design not described in sources

brand_strength.rationale: Trademarks were registered for the word mark and an image mark, but no press, community or founder interview about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Furmacy, a Winter 2021 YC veterinary e-prescribing company co-founded by a veterinarian, was sold to Wag! Group in an all-stock deal that closed 2022-10-24 for about $283 thousand in shares per Wag!'s SEC filing, roughly 20 months after the batch. The tiny price and the later closure of its pharmacy suggest a soft landing rather than a venture-scale exit, though the filing does not state the reason. A CB Insights entry that lists MWI Animal Health in July 2025 is unconfirmed and may reflect a later transfer or a data error.
notes: Earlier depth-1 record named MWI Animal Health (2025) as acquirer from one CB Insights snippet; the Wag! SEC filing (primary source) shows the 2022-10-24 acquisition, and Madrimasd also lists Wag!. MWI 2025 entry stays unverified. Funding: CB Insights says $130K total over 5 rounds and Madrimasd lists Grant Park Ventures and Eppes Creek Ventures (seed, 2021-04) but amounts are unverified, so no rounds recorded; funding_data_coverage none_found. furmacy.com did not resolve in this session. Wag! acquisition value is the share value stated in the filing, not necessarily cash paid. Name origin is an inference from a USPTO pseudo mark ('FUR PHARMACY'), not stated by the company, so name_origin left null. No dated competitor sources from 2020-21 found; Covetrus vRxPro (2024) is later and not listed. failure_factors acquihire_soft_landing is a judgment from price and closure, not a stated reason.
